method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **SVT is common in infancy and childhood**, usually re-entrant, in otherwise well children. **More than a third of new-onset SVT occurs in the first few weeks of life**, often presenting after many hours with heart failure.
claims.source_text: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is common in infancy and childhood. Most SVT in children is due to a re-entrant mechanism and usually occurs in otherwise normally well children … Greater than a third of new onset SVT occurs in the first few weeks of life, commonly presenting after many hours with signs of heart failure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Younger children: usually AVRT** (including Wolff-Parkinson-White). **Adolescents: more often AVNRT.**
claims.source_text: Younger children: usually caused by atrioventricular re-entry (AVRT), including Wolff-Parkinson White syndrome … Adolescents: more commonly caused by atrioventricular nodal re-entry (AVNRT)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SVT has a fixed rate, usually over 220 bpm**, with abrupt onset and offset; P-waves are not visible or sit after the QRS.
claims.source_text: SVT typically has a fixed rate, usually >220 bpm. Onset and offset are abrupt, and p-waves are either not visible or seen after the QRS complexes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Assume a broad-complex tachycardia is VT**, not SVT with aberrancy, unless there is clear evidence it is not VT.
claims.source_text: Always assume a broad complex tachycardia is due to VT rather than SVT with aberrancy, unless there is clear evidence it is not VT
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for and address contributors**: sepsis, pain, dehydration, anxiety and fever.
claims.source_text: Factors that may contribute to tachycardia (eg sepsis, pain, dehydration, anxiety, and fever) should also be considered and addressed when managing a patient presenting with a tachyarrhythmia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infants tolerate it well and present late** — irritability, poor feeding, lethargy, sweating, then congestive heart failure. **Older children feel palpitations and present earlier**, often with a normal examination.
claims.source_text: Infants Children/Adolescents Feature Tolerate tachycardia well, making early signs and symptoms initially subtle Able to perceive palpitations and therefore present earlier with less clinical signs or symptoms History Parental concern for infant Irritability, poor feeding, lethargy and sweating Child complains of feeling ill, breathless, chest pain, nausea, dizziness or sweating Examination Typically present late, with signs of congestive heart failure (respiratory distress, hepatomegaly, oedema) Examination may be normal
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Identify the child in shock** (pallor, poor perfusion, decreased consciousness, hypotension) **and resuscitate immediately.** Red flags: unwell appearance, hypotension, drowsiness. **BP machines and oximeters may be unreliable at SVT rates.**
claims.source_text: The priority is to identify the child in shock (pallor, poor perfusion, decreased consciousness, hypotension) and proceed immediately to resuscitation … Red Flags Unwell appearance, hypotension, drowsiness/altered conscious state … Note: BP machines and pulse oximeters may be unreliable at common SVT rates
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **12-lead ECG before and after reversion.** CXR only if heart failure signs; **blood tests are not recommended** unless considering other causes.
claims.source_text: 12 lead ECG (pre and post reversion techniques) … CXR can be considered if clinical signs of heart failure present … Blood tests provide no added benefit to the diagnosis or management and therefore are not recommended, unless considering other causes of SVT
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sinus tachycardia:** under 220, normal P-waves, variable rate, unwell child. **SVT:** over 220 (commonly 250–300 in infants), P-waves absent or after the QRS, fixed rate.
claims.source_text: Sinus Tachycardia <220 Present, normal morphology Variable Typically unwell children or systemic illness Supra Ventricular Tachycardia >220 (commonly 250-300 in infants) Absent or after QRS Fixed
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Atrial flutter** reaches up to 500/min in neonates (300/min in children); sawtooth waves are often seen only with adenosine-induced AV block. **Atrial ectopic tachycardia** may not respond to DC cardioversion or adenosine and can cause cardiomyopathy. **Junctional ectopic tachycardia:** 170–300, post cardiac surgery.
claims.source_text: Atrial Flutter Up to 500 beats/min in neonates (300 beats/min in children) with variable AV conduction being common Saw tooth flutter waves (often only appreciated with AV block from adenosine) … Atrial Ectopic Tachycardia Precede QRS with abnormal axis Variable May not respond to DC cardioversion or adenosine. Can cause cardiomyopathy. … Junctional Ectopic Tachycardia 170-300 Inverted Variable Post cardiac surgery
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Only in a clinically stable child, on continuous cardiac monitoring.** If unsuccessful or the child deteriorates, move to medical treatment.
claims.source_text: Vagal manoeuvres should only be attempted in a child who is clinically stable … Continuous cardiac monitoring should be applied prior to performing … If unsuccessful, or child deteriorates, proceed to medical treatment as per the algorithm
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do NOT use eyeball pressure or carotid sinus massage.**
claims.source_text: DO NOT perform Eyeball pressure or carotid sinus massage as they are no longer recommended
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Under 6 months: facial immersion in ice water for 5 seconds** (diving reflex) — no need to occlude the nostrils; safe and 90% effective.
claims.source_text: Neonates and infants (<6 months) ‘Elicit the diving reflex’ with facial immersion in ice water for 5 seconds … It is unnecessary to occlude the nostrils … This technique is safe and 90% effective in terminating SVT
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never use facial immersion in an infant with haemodynamic compromise or shock.**
claims.source_text: Facial immersion must not be used for infants in hemodynamic compromise/shock
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Older infants and toddlers:** ice-cold facecloth or bag of ice slurry to the face for 15–30 seconds.
claims.source_text: Older infants / Toddlers Apply an ice-cold facecloth or bag filled with ice slurry to the face for 15-30 seconds (elicits the ‘dive reflex’).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **School-aged children: Valsalva** — supine, blow into a thumb or 10 mL syringe after full inspiration for 10–15 seconds, visibly straining with no air escape.
claims.source_text: School-aged children Valsalva technique: with the child in the supine position, ask them to blow on their thumb or a 10 mL syringe, after full inspiration, for 10-15 seconds. … There should be no air escape and the child should be seen to strain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Modified Valsalva is more effective:** strain semi-recumbent, then lie flat immediately with passive leg raise to 45 degrees.
claims.source_text: Modified Valsalva: manoeuvre performed as above in a semi-recumbent position. Then at the end of the strain, the child is immediately repositioned into a supine position with passive leg raise to 45 degrees. … This has been demonstrated to significantly increase efficacy of the Valsalva manoeuvre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adenosine's half-life is 5–10 seconds**; it briefly blocks the AV node. **Always record a rhythm strip during it** — the response helps diagnosis even if SVT doesn't terminate.
claims.source_text: Adenosine has a very short half-life of 5-10 seconds. It acts by briefly blocking AV node conduction … Always attempt to record a rhythm strip during adenosine administration as the response may be helpful in the diagnosis of the underlying tachycardia even if the tachycardia does not terminate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Flushing and chest tightness are common.** ⚠️ **It can exacerbate asthma — avoid with a history of severe asthma or active wheeze.**
claims.source_text: Transient flushing and chest tightness/discomfort are relatively common side effects … Exacerbation of asthma due to bronchospasm (avoid in patients with history of severe asthma or active wheeze at time of experiencing SVT)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lower dose with dipyridamole; avoid if possible after cardiac transplant** (asystole, bradycardia — lower dose and consult cardiology if used). **Children on theophylline need higher doses** — consult cardiology.
claims.source_text: Adenosine contraindications: Patients taking dipyridamole (Persantin) require a lower dose of adenosine … For post cardiac transplant patients with a denervated heart, adenosine should be avoided if possible (risk of asystole or sustained bradycardia). If used, a lower dose is required. Consult cardiology … For children on theophylline, consult cardiology. Theophylline competes at the adenosine receptor and therefore children on this medication will require higher doses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Adenosine can turn re-entry SVT into atrial fibrillation — dangerous with WPW, needs DC cardioversion.** Rapid re-initiation is not uncommon; discuss with cardiology.
claims.source_text: Beware of Adenosine changing re-entry SVT to atrial fibrillation, which can be dangerous if WPW is present. This will require DC cardioversion … Rapid re-initiation of tachycardia is not uncommon, mostly due to premature atrial contractions stimulated by the adenosine. If this occurs, discuss with Cardiology
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Verapamil is contraindicated under 12 months** (irreversible hypotension, lethal ventricular dysfunction) and is not routinely used in children.
claims.source_text: Verapamil Contraindicated in children <12 months, due to irreversible hypotension and lethal ventricular dysfunction … Not routinely used in children, despite increasing use of calcium-channel blockade in adults for the management of SVT
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Often needs admission:** first presentation · under 3 months · heart failure · needed DC conversion.
claims.source_text: The child with the following often requires admission: first presentation under 3 months of age in heart failure requiring DC conversion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Known SVT with a breakthrough episode:** discuss with the child's usual cardiology team.
claims.source_text: Children with known SVT having a breakthrough episode should be discussed with their usual Cardiology team where possible
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge once reverted, not meeting admission criteria, and observed for 90 minutes**, with follow-up arranged.
claims.source_text: The child has reverted, not meeting the criteria for review/admission above, and observed for 90 min. Ensure follow up arranged
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT' (Last updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Supraventricular_Tachycardia_SVT/, retrieved 2026-09-23
